prompt: Mid-case: The client is deciding whether to buy a delivery van. You've found that it costs $40,000 and would save $10,000 a year in courier fees. You haven't looked at running costs. Which is the best summary?

options.text: So far: the van pays back in 4 years including all its costs. Next I'd choose a model.
options.feedback: This claims findings the analysis hasn't shown. Summarize only what you've established.

options.text: So far: the van costs $40,000 and saves $10,000 a year in courier fees, a 4-year payback before running costs. The van comes in three colors. Next I'd add running costs to see if the payback still works.
options.feedback: It leads with the answer, but pads it with a fact that doesn't bear on the decision.

options.text: So far: the van would save money on couriers. Next I'd add running costs to see if the payback still works.
options.feedback: It gives an answer but none of the numbers from the fact sheet to back it.

options.text: So far: the van costs $40,000 and saves $10,000 a year in courier fees, a 4-year payback before running costs. We haven't yet looked at running costs such as fuel, insurance and a driver, so next I'd add running costs to see if the payback still works.
options.feedback: Right. It states what is known, with numbers, then what is still open and what comes next.

explanation: The van costs $40,000 and saves $10,000 a year in courier fees, a 4-year payback before running costs. A good mid-case summary states what is known with numbers and what comes next, without claiming findings that haven't been tested.

irrelevant_facts: The van comes in three colors.
